clue.text: Basic study covered by group banned at first, say

indicators.note: the study word sits wrapped inside the group word, which covers it

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians for instance
to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: only the opening letter of banned is wanted here

parts.note: to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A basic study gets swallowed up by a group that was banned at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' signals a container, and 'at first' takes just the opening letter of 'banned'; 'say' looks like an example marker but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread-and-butter issues are the basic, everyday essentials, an idiom for fundamental matters.

clue.text: Aspirin habits developed, quietly supporting two parties

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, so it comes last
the letters of aspirin habits are developed into a new arrangement

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone's aspirin habit develops quietly while they back both political sides.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supporting' puts P below the anagram of ASPIRIN HABITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipartisanship is cooperation involving the two main political parties, so the clue words stand loosely for it.

clue.text: Finished taking old women for granted

indicators.note: the finished word takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: something finished has ended

explanation.surface: Having finished, someone takes old women for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For granted' looks like the idiom; 'granted' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Endowed means given or bestowed, so it is a synonym of granted in the sense of being provided with something.

clue.text: Intending to keep home counties, getting control

indicators.note: the intending phrase keeps the counties' letters held inside it

parts.note: what you are driving at is what you intend, so driving at means intending
the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: Someone plans to keep hold of the counties near London and so take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South East (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the driving seat is an idiom for being in charge, having control of a situation.

clue.text: Understand after weapon turned up — valuable little piece

indicators.note: the understand word comes after the weapon piece
in a down clue, turned up means the weapon word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: Someone grasps what happens after a weapon is raised, finding something precious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses GUN to NUG in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump of gold, or figuratively a small valuable piece of information.

clue.text: Raise barrel and lock for support

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the barrel word lifts it so it reads upwards

parts.note: a tub is a barrel-like container
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Instructions for propping things up: lift a barrel and secure it with a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' reverses TUB to BUT in the down entry; 'barrel' is not BUTT.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a structure built against a wall to brace it, so it is a support.

clue.text: X may be the one regularly going missing

indicators.note: every other letter of the one goes missing, leaving the rest at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the letter X standing for the one that keeps disappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of THE ONE. X is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: X is the Roman numeral for the number after nine, the quantity the answer names.

clue.text: Look from European disgusting you at one time?

parts.note: vile means disgusting
ye is an old form of you, used at one time

explanation.surface: A disgusted glance from a European directed at you long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent glance, believed to cast a curse, so it is a kind of look.

clue.text: Take on challenge sent Telegraph mad — about time!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about the time letter, holding it inside
mad suggests the letters of sent telegraph are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A rebellious challenge drove the Telegraph mad, and it was about time.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SENT TELEGRAPH, signalled by 'mad', goes 'about' T.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp the nettle is an idiom for tackling a difficult problem boldly, taking on a challenge.

clue.text: Drop answer in superfluous material for university course

indicators.note: the answer letter is dropped from the padding word
the university letter goes in place of the one dropped

parts.note: padding is superfluous material added to fill out writing

explanation.surface: Advice to cut the padding from an essay for a university course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'university course' looks like one phrase, but 'course' is the definition: a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding is the dessert course of a meal, in British usage.

clue.text: City that might see Iran get jumpy?

indicators.note: jumpy suggests the letters of Iran get leap about into a new order

explanation.surface: A city where Iran might become nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a port city in northern Morocco, on the Strait of Gibraltar.

clue.text: Particularly sensitive due to return of hostilities

indicators.note: the return of the hostilities word means reading it backwards

parts.note: war means hostilities

explanation.surface: Feelings are tender because fighting has broken out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw describes something sore and tender, such as a raw nerve or raw emotions.

clue.text: Picks, for example, remedies for tension

definitions.meaning: ice picks are tools that break up ice
things that ease awkwardness when strangers first meet, like party games

explanation.surface: Tools such as picks double as cures for strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, tools that break ice; figuratively, activities that relieve social tension, a well-known idiom.

clue.text: Reach workers absorbed by craft set-up

indicators.note: the reach and workers pieces are absorbed inside the craft word

parts.note: art is a craft or skill
range means reach, as in the reach of a gun
men are workers, as in a firm's men

explanation.surface: Workers reach a ship and are taken aboard as part of an organised plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed by' puts the pieces inside the craft word, after its second letter rather than its first.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement is the way things are organised, synonymous with a set-up.

clue.text: Dye most of the subcontinent try

indicators.note: most of the subcontinent's name is kept, with its last letter cut

parts.note: India is called the subcontinent
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: A dye sourced from most of India, which you should try.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue dye, originally obtained from plants grown in India.

clue.text: Hungry new entries will accept uniform

indicators.note: the scrambled letters will accept the uniform letter inside them
new indicates the letters of entries are made into a fresh order

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: New recruits are hungry and ready to accept their uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals the anagram of ENTRIES, and 'will accept' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word meaning greedy or ravenously eager to eat.

clue.text: Commercial breeding ground for schools?

parts.note: schools of fish are raised commercially at a hatchery business, not schools of children

explanation.surface: A business that turns out educational institutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' suggests education; here it means groups of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm breeds fish commercially, and fish swim in schools.

clue.text: Order that might follow main course?

definitions.text: Order that might follow main course?

parts.words: Order that might follow main course?
parts.note: ... order means perfect neatness, and a fruit pastry might come after the main course of a meal

explanation.surface: Something a diner might ask for after the main dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a diner's request; it is also the 'order' of the idiom apple-pie order.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple pie is a typical dessert after a main course, and apple-pie order means perfect tidiness.

clue.text: Planned reception, missing church source of energy

indicators.note: planned suggests the letters of reception are rearranged into a design
the church letters are missing from the reception letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A planned reception goes ahead without a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C and E from RECEPTION ('missing church') and rearrange the rest ('Planned').
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is a nutrient the body can burn for fuel, so it is a dietary energy source.

clue.text: Course offering right of admission

definitions.meaning: a dish served at a meal, the main dish in American usage or a starter in British
the right or freedom to enter a place or social circle

explanation.surface: A dish that gets you in the door.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a dish within a meal, and also a means of access to a group or place.

clue.text: Regret broadcast and gibe? Nonsense!

indicators.note: broadcast means the regret word is heard spoken, not read

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a barb is a cutting remark, a gibe

explanation.surface: Someone regrets broadcasting a taunt and is dismissed as talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: RHU is said like RUE. Rhubarb is also the word actors mutter to sound like crowd noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense or meaningless talk.

clue.text: Correctly placed amid no-win situation

indicators.note: the letters sit amid the words no-win situation

explanation.surface: Something positioned properly in the middle of a hopeless predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for in its original or proper place.

clue.text: Unexpectedly convert cheat

parts.note: taken short or caught short means caught unexpectedly
to change something is to convert it

explanation.surface: A sudden conversion turns out to be a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convert' looks like an anagram signal; it is just CHANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To short-change someone is to give too little money back, so it means to cheat.

clue.text: Instrument of torture ultimately found by kingdom

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of torture

explanation.surface: A torture device turns up in a kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument of torture' looks like one phrase; 'Instrument' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Uke is short for ukulele, a small four-stringed musical instrument.

clue.text: Sloth at home has it back in time

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the reversed it goes inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: back means the word it is turned round

explanation.surface: A sloth lazing at home with its back turned for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns 'it' round, and 'in' puts the turned word inside the period of time; 'has' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to do nothing, a synonym of sloth meaning laziness.

clue.text: Thanks — but discovered this letter

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: dis-covered means the covering outer letters are stripped from but

explanation.surface: Someone says thanks, but then reveals a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Some excused from new income taxes? That's not all right!

indicators.note: the letters of some are excused, let off, from the pool
new signals the remaining letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Some people are exempt from the latest income taxes, which is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, O, M, E from INCOME TAXES ('excused from') and rearrange ('new') what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is imprecise or slightly wrong, so not quite correct.

clue.text: Impossible horse inside able to be covered!

indicators.note: the horse word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: insurable means able to be covered by insurance
a mount is a horse that is ridden

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a horse inside could actually be insured.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurmountable means unable to be overcome, which in context means impossible.
